nodes.name: 3-Axis Acceleration Sensing
responsibilities: Measure raw acceleration along the X, Y, and Z axes using the MPU6050 IMU (user-stated constraint).
Maintain the sensor in an active measurement state.
Make digitized acceleration register values available for retrieval over I2C (user-stated constraint).

nodes.name: I2C Communication Interface
responsibilities: Manage the I2C bus protocol between the processing subsystem and the MPU6050 (user-stated constraint).
Issue read transactions to retrieve raw acceleration register data from the sensor.
Handle addressing, timing, and acknowledgement required by the I2C protocol.

nodes.name: Acceleration Data Processing
responsibilities: Receive raw 16-bit acceleration register values from the I2C interface.
Convert raw register values into meaningful acceleration quantities for all three axes (X, Y, Z).
Exclude gyroscope and all other MPU6050 output channels from processing (user-stated constraint).
Format the three-axis acceleration values into a human-readable serial output string.
Orchestrate the periodic read-process-transmit cycle running on the ESP32 DevKit (user-stated constraint).

nodes.name: Serial Output Transmission
responsibilities: Transmit formatted X/Y/Z acceleration strings to the connected laptop over a serial (UART-to-USB) link.
Maintain the serial link at a baud rate compatible with standard laptop serial monitors.
Ensure each transmission is complete and delimited so the laptop terminal can display discrete readings.

nodes.name: Laptop Serial Monitor
responsibilities: Receive serial data from the device over USB.
Display the streamed X/Y/Z acceleration values to the user in real time.

nodes.name: Power Supply
responsibilities: Deliver regulated power to the processing subsystem and the sensing subsystem.
Accept power from an external source (e.g., USB from the laptop or a dedicated supply).

edges.description: Regulated power delivered to the acceleration sensing subsystem to keep the MPU6050 active.
Regulated power delivered to the processing subsystem (ESP32 DevKit) to sustain operation.
Processing subsystem initiates I2C read transactions on a periodic basis, controlling the communication interface.
I2C interface issues register-read commands to the sensing subsystem to trigger data retrieval.
Raw 16-bit acceleration register values for X, Y, and Z axes returned from the sensing subsystem over I2C.

Serial (UART-over-USB) stream of formatted acceleration readings transmitted from the device to the laptop serial monitor.
